findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty/undefined and location is Google Meet
findings.body: In EventManager.create, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` dereferences without optional chaining. When a booking has no destination calendars (evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array — which is now the normal case for users without a destination calendar, e.g. handleNewBooking sets null), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this line throws a TypeError, failing the whole booking creation whenever Google Meet is selected as location. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and was null-safe.

findings.title: Patch after insert uses possibly-undefined calendarId
findings.body: In createEvent, the insert call falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the subsequent events.patch (used to add the hangout link to the description) passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the fallback. When no destinationCalendar matches the credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined and the patch request is sent with calendarId undefined, so the description/hangoutLink update silently fails (or errors) for every event created on the primary calendar.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent lose destination calendar fallback for legacy bookings
findings.body: In updateEvent the new code is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is null/undefined (all bookings created before the externalCalendarId reference refactor, and any reference where it wasn't stored), the `.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares against null/undefined and never matches, so selectedCalendar is undefined. The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The same broken pattern exists in deleteEvent (line 315-317). Result: updating or cancelling legacy Google bookings calls the API with calendarId undefined, which fails or hits the wrong calendar, so events on a non-primary destination calendar are never updated/deleted.

findings.title: Organizer attendee email always set from first destination calendar, even when creating on another host's calendar
findings.body: createEvent always uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` (the first entry of destinationCalendar) as the organizer attendee email. In the multi-host collective scenario this PR targets, the same event is created once per destination calendar with different credentials; for the second host's calendar the organizer email will still be the first host's externalId, producing a wrong organizer on that event and potentially bouncing attendee invites. The email should be derived from the destination matching the current credentialId (the `selectedCalendar`), not unconditionally from the first array entry.

findings.title: Unrelated inversion of IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED slug condition
findings.body: The diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This inverts when the org team gets a slug: previously the slug was set when team billing was NOT enabled and requestedSlug when it WAS; now slug is set when billing IS enabled. This is unrelated to the destinationCalendar work and silently changes organization subdomain creation behavior for self-hosted (non-billing) instances, which will now never get a slug set on team creation.

findings.title: Lark/CalDav/Office365 services ignore per-destination calendars for multi-host events
findings.body: LarkCalendarService.createEvent (and BaseCalendarService in packages/lib/CalendarService.ts line 156, and Office365CalendarService line 73) still only read the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`). EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now iterates all destinations and calls createEvent per credential, but these services always create the event on the first host's calendar regardless of which destination/credential is being processed, so secondary hosts on Lark/CalDav/Office365 will either get duplicate events on the wrong calendar or no event on their own calendar — the exact bug this PR claims to fix, only fixed for Google Calendar.

findings.title: credentialId dropped from video references in create()
findings.body: In `referencesToCreate` inside create(), `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` discards the credentialId for video results. Previously it fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId` for non-calendar results. While the old fallback was also wrong (it used the calendar's credential for video), the new code stores no credentialId at all for video references, which handleCancelBooking relies on (`bookingVideoReference.credentialId`) to find the video credential and delete the meeting on cancellation — cancelled bookings with video meetings will now leak the video meeting. createMeeting's EventResult should carry and propagate the video credential's id.

findings.title: Only the first destination calendar is persisted on the booking
findings.body: When creating the booking, `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined` connects only the first destination calendar (the DB relation is single). For collective events, secondary hosts' destination calendars are only recoverable via the created bookingReferences; any code path that rebuilds a CalendarEvent from the booking (cancel, reschedule, requestReschedule, payment webhooks — all updated in this PR to `[booking.destinationCalendar]`) will only include the organizer's calendar. If reference creation fails or a reference lacks externalCalendarId, secondary hosts' calendar events become orphaned. Consider persisting all destinations or ensuring the fallback paths reconstruct the full list.

findings.title: Error message in updateAllCalendarEvents catch no longer logged
findings.body: The catch block previously did `console.error(message)`; the new code builds the same detailed message (including which credential/book failed) but never logs or reports it — it's only used in a template that is discarded. Failures inside updateAllCalendarEvents are now silent apart from the synthesized failure results, making production debugging of calendar update failures harder.
